reason: A shrinks both decorative circles. The top-right one now floats loose inside the canvas, crowding the can, instead of bleeding off the edge, so the original's framing is lost. All the content is packed into the top 70%, leaving a big dead band between the CTA and the tiny legal line, which sits awkwardly beside the shrunken bottom circle. B keeps the large circles bleeding off the edges as in the original, and the logo, can, headline and CTA stack is better centred vertically. Its flaws: the GLACIER logo now sits fully on top of the circle, the top margin is oversized, and the small, hard-to-read legal text floats at mid-low height on the edge of the bottom circle instead of being anchored to the bottom.

A: the SOLSTICE wordmark is jammed against the bottle cap and the canvas top edge. The subtitle is tiny, the headline is undersized for the banner, and there are dead gaps between the bottle, text and button, so it reads like a shrunken copy. B has a strong headline and a clear CTA and follows the banner's left-to-right reading order, but it is cramped: the headline's 'z' runs into the decorative circles, the two circles overlap each other awkwardly, the subtitle wraps into three ragged lines, and the button sits close to the right edge.

A has no collisions, but its hierarchy is broken. The CTA button and 'Ships late June' are tiny and unreadable, the body copy is far larger than the CTA, the legal block is as big as the button, and the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow is gone. B is unusable: the eyebrow sits on top of the SOLSTICE logo, the orange divider cuts through the headline's last line, and the headline's last line overlaps the body copy, so the text in that area can't be read.

A: the headline is shrunk into two long lines that almost touch the side edges. There is a big, pointless gap between the headline and the CTA, and the bottom ~280px is dead space, so the layout looks top-heavy and unfinished. B: the headline is large and fills the portrait canvas, with good line breaks and a clear hierarchy above the CTA. The stack sits a bit low, though: the top margin (~170px) is much bigger than the bottom margin under the button (~50px), so it needs vertical rebalancing.

A: the left edges don't line up (the headline starts at about x=64 while SOLSTICE, the subhead and the pills start at x=76). The headline runs almost to the right edge, and the CTA floats between the copy and the pills, so the reading order is copy → button → flavour pills, cut off from the button. B: a clean left-aligned column with a logical order, but the headline box is narrow for no reason, leaving the single word 'here' alone on the second line. The right half is largely empty dead space, with the cluster jammed to the left.

A breaks the product badge apart: the cream circle sits clipped in the bottom-left corner, separate from the can. The can body is orange on orange, so it turns into an invisible ghost outline. The headline is also small and floats among scattered elements with no grid. B keeps the logo, headline, NEW pill and CTA intact with a clear hierarchy. However, everything is packed into the top half and the bottom ~45% is empty, the NEW pill and CTA float in a separate right column, and the product circle is crammed into the top-left corner.

A is broken: the 'See the Schedule' button is cut off at the bottom edge and its label spills past the pill. The body copy is nearly as large as the headline, which flattens the hierarchy. The card fills the canvas edge to edge, so there are no margins and the confetti is reduced to a thin border. A also drops the legal line and leaves the logo squeezed into a corner beside the book. B keeps the book over the confetti on the left and a card on the right with a clear headline > body > CTA hierarchy and the legal text kept next to the button. B's flaws: the Inkwell & Lantern logo is tiny and barely legible, the book is undersized, the kicker floats top-right away from the logo, the legal text is cramped beside the CTA, and the card runs close to the top and bottom edges.

Candidate A is broken. The headline's wrapped 'week' runs into the subhead ('audio coaching'). The legal text is jammed directly under the subhead, and the yearly card's 'per year' spills out of its dark card as cream text on a light background, so it can't be read. The headline is also small, so it doesn't stand out over the cards. Candidate B has a strong, clean headline and a clear CTA with no collisions, but it has real faults. The price cards are shrunk so far that the plan names and 'per month/year' labels can't be read. The cards are reordered to 6/80/48, which breaks the original Monthly-Yearly-Family order and moves the featured yearly plan off-centre. The subhead and legal text are crammed into a tiny block at the right edge.

A turns the decorative circles into large discs that sit fully on the canvas instead of bleeding off the corners, and the GLACIER wordmark and the can now sit on top of the teal disc, so the background competes with the logo. A's legal line also floats in mid-air across the light-blue disc, with dead space below it. B keeps the logo and product on clean background and puts the legal text at the bottom, but its shrunken circles read as arbitrary floating dots. The teal disc almost touches the can's right green dot, and there is a large empty band between the CTA and the legal text.

A uses a clear left-to-right banner order (logo, bottle, headline/body, CTA) with a strong headline, but it is crowded: 'fizz' runs into the stacked decorative circles, the CTA pill and the bottle sit almost against the canvas edges, and the body copy wraps to three ragged lines. B leaves more space and centres the headline well, but the SOLSTICE logo is squeezed against the top edge and almost touches the bottle cap, the bottle runs nearly edge to edge on the left, the body copy is shrunk to barely readable, and the centre band sits between empty areas.

A is badly broken: the last headline lines run into the body copy, the orange divider cuts through 'Orange Zest and Smoked', and the 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow is jammed against the dark header band. That leaves it unreadable and unshippable. B has no collisions, but its hierarchy is wrong. The 'Reserve a Case' CTA has shrunk to a tiny, illegible pill, while the body copy is huge and competes with the headline. The eyebrow is missing, and the legal text and 'Ships late June' are microscopic and crowded into the right column.

A reflows the headline to four large lines, keeps the original look and puts the CTA right under it, so it fills the portrait canvas well. Its only flaw is that the group sits low: about 170px of space at the top against about 50px under the CTA. B squeezes the headline into two undersized lines that nearly touch the side edges (about 40px margins) and leaves a disconnected gap above the CTA. The whole group floats in the upper half, leaving about 40% dead orange space at the bottom.

A keeps a clean shared left edge and a sensible order (brand → headline → subcopy → pills → CTA), but the headline wraps with 'here' orphaned on its own line, the right half and bottom band are mostly empty, and the cut-off peach circle sits off on its own. B fails on several points. The headline runs almost to the right edge and doesn't line up with the left edge of SOLSTICE and the subcopy. The CTA floats off to the right between the subcopy and the pills, so the flavour pills end up below the button and the reading order breaks. The headline and subcopy also sit partly on top of the big circle, and the layout feels random and cramped.

A keeps the product badge intact and the headline dominant, but every element is packed into the top ~60% and leaves a large empty orange band below. The NEW pill and Try It button sit in an awkward right column on a different axis from the headline, so the layout looks top-heavy and unfinished. B breaks the product graphic: the cream circle is detached and pushed into the bottom-left corner, and the orange can now blends into the orange background, leaving only a faint outline. B's headline is also small and weak, and the subcopy, CTA and NEW pill are scattered on unrelated axes, so its hierarchy and fidelity collapse.

A uses the banner shape sensibly: book cover on the left, card on the right with a strong headline and a full CTA. Its flaws: the Inkwell & Lantern logo is shrunk to an almost unreadable mark crammed into the card's top-left corner, the fine print sits beside the CTA at nearly body size and competes with it, and the book cover is small and isolated on the busy confetti. B's 'See the Schedule' CTA runs off the bottom-left edge of the canvas and is clipped, the body copy is crammed against it, the eyebrow is spaced out awkwardly, and the logo sits in the top-right with no clear relationship to the book. Losing the call to action makes B clearly broken.

A: the headline and CTA carry the banner well. But the price cards are shrunk to thumbnails with unreadable labels, and their order is shuffled to 6/80/48, which breaks the original sequence. The legal text and subhead are packed into a cramped column against the right edge, and the logo is tiny. B is worse: the headline's second line 'week' collides with the subhead. The 'per month', 'per year' and 'up to 5 people' labels spill outside their cards, and 'per year' is pale cream on a light background, so it is almost invisible. The legal text is illegibly small.

A is the better resize. It keeps the original's layered composition, with the green circle behind the bag and the bag big enough to fill the tall format. Its flaws: the headline wraps so that 'fizz' sits alone on the second line, the CTA is jammed close under the headline, and the olive circle is cut off in the bottom-left corner. B shrinks everything. The CITRINE logo and the 'Find a Store' button text are tiny and hard to read, and the headline is weak for this size. The green circle has been pulled off the product and floats at the bottom beside the olive one, which leaves an awkward pile of decoration at the bottom and dead space around the small headline and button.

A works as a left-to-right banner: the wordmark, headline, body and badges share one left edge, and the CTA stands alone on the right. Its flaws are an orphaned 'and bottles.' line, an oversized dead gap between the headline and the body, and a circle that almost touches the top and bottom edges. B's GLACIER wordmark floats centred and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge. Its body copy and CTA are jammed against the bottom edge, and the circle crowds the canvas edges. The right-hand badge and CTA cluster also feels disconnected from the copy.

A centres the headline but left-aligns the CTA, so the two blocks don't share an axis. Its line break leaves 'sunshine.' alone on the second line, and the LIMITED badge has moved from before the button to after it, a different arrangement from the original. B keeps the original's centred composition and badge-plus-button pairing with a balanced two-line headline, but the headline sits too close to the top edge, leaving a lopsided empty band at the bottom, and the 'LIMITED' text on the badge is tiny.

A inverts the hierarchy: the 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' attribution is set larger and bolder than the quote, the quote sits in the middle as tiny text, and the Solstice logo is dropped entirely. B keeps the quote as the main left-aligned text with a modest quote mark, and it keeps the logo and the product. Its flaws are that the attribution floats far from its quote in the top-centre, the logo is a tiny orphaned element under it, and the quote text is barely legible at 50px tall.

A shrinks the text badly: the CITRINE wordmark and the 'Find a Store' button label are tiny and hard to read at this size. Its two decorative circles are pulled off the edges and parked as floating balls in the bottom corners, so they look like stray dots instead of the original's edge-bleeding shapes, and there is a large dead band above the headline. B keeps the edge-bleeding circle layout and readable sizes for the logo, headline and CTA, but the headline wraps with 'fizz' left alone on line two, the button sits too close to the headline, and the bottom third feels empty.

A: the GLACIER wordmark floats centred near x≈330 and doesn't line up with the headline's left edge at x≈195. The badges and CTA sit in a separate right column that runs almost to the bottom edge, and the body copy is pushed into the bottom-left corner, so the whole thing reads as scattered pieces. B: the wordmark, headline, body copy and badges share one clean left edge, and the CTA sits as a clear endpoint on the right, which suits the banner format. Its flaws are a big dead gap between the headline and the body copy, the body copy wrapping to leave 'and bottles.' on a short last line, and badges jammed near the bottom edge.

A keeps the original's centred headline and the LIMITED badge + CTA cluster, and the headline wraps more evenly. However, the headline sits close to the top edge, leaving extra empty space at the bottom, and the CTA cluster is slightly off the headline's centre axis, as it was in the original. B wraps the headline badly, leaving 'sunshine.' alone on the second line. Its CTA is pushed to the left margin while the headline stays centred, so the two share no alignment, and the LIMITED badge now trails after the button and looks oversized, which breaks the original's grouping and hierarchy.

A reads left to right as a banner should: quote mark, quote, attribution, SOLSTICE logo, then the can. It keeps the brand logo. Its flaws: the attribution floats far from the quote, at the top centre-right with dead space under it, and the quote text and can are tiny. B gets the hierarchy wrong: the bold gold attribution, pushed into the bottom-left corner, is bigger and louder than the quote and comes before it in reading order. B also drops the SOLSTICE logo and leaves the can as a small, cramped scrap at the right edge.

A: the headline is barely bigger than the body copy, so the hierarchy falls apart. The left column (logo, sale ribbon, small can) is cramped, while the right column has no shared edge: the headline is centred, the CTA is offset to the left and the legal text drifts right, with dead space underneath. B: the large two-line headline gives it strong hierarchy and a sensible banner layout. Its flaws: the product is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail in the top-right corner, the body copy wraps with a short orphan line ('on June 21.'), the CTA almost touches the right edge, and the headline sits tight to the bottom edge.

A has a strong, readable headline and fills the portrait canvas well, but the alignment is mixed: GROVE is centred, the headline and body are flush left, and the pills and CTA are pushed right, so there is no common edge. The bottom cluster is also tight. B has weak hierarchy: the headline is small and sits above an odd large gap before the body, which leaves an orphaned 'bottles.' line. The FREE DELIVERY badge floats loose beside the pills, the shoe sits high in its circle, and about 140px of dead space is left at the bottom.

A is the original scaled into the square. It's clean and keeps the hierarchy and reading order, but the text block is too small for the canvas and sits slightly high, leaving large empty orange bands above and below, so it reads as a shrunk copy rather than a rearrangement. B gives the headline real presence, but its bottom row is weak: the subcopy is centre-wrapped awkwardly ('Now in / four flavours.') and sits beside the CTA instead of above it, which breaks the headline-copy-action order. Neither the subcopy nor the CTA lines up with the headline's edges (the CTA runs past the headline's right edge), and the row is cramped against the bottom compared with the open space above.

A: the bottle sits on top of the text column. It covers '20% off' and cuts the body copy off at 'case of' and 'sparklin', and the bottom third of the canvas is dead space. B: a clean vertical stack with no collisions, but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow has dropped below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order. The left-aligned text block also clashes with the centred bottle and CTA, and the headline is crammed against the edge of the circle.

A: everything sits in the top two-thirds. The phone is small and jammed near the top edge, and the bottom band is dead, empty space. The ONLINE ONLY badge is stacked awkwardly under the Try It button, so the CTA cluster reads as a loose afterthought. B: it fills the format better and the headline and CTA have strong hierarchy. But the Try It button and badge are crammed into the bottom-right corner almost touching the bottom edge, the badge crowds the subcopy, and the phone's backing circle is clipped at the left edge.

A keeps the original left-to-right order of product badge, headline and CTA. However, 'Out now.' sits far below the headline with a big gap, the 'Try It' pill floats in the middle of that gap and almost touches the headline, and the pill sits only about 18px from the right edge of the canvas. B breaks up the original layout: the 'Out now.' subline is pulled away from its headline and placed beside the button, and the button butts directly against the bottom of the product circle. All the weight is crammed into the right half while the lower left is dead space, so the reading order runs from headline to product to CTA and then back to the subline.

A: the tilted can sits on top of the 'Pier 9' venue text, which is a clear collision. The subtitle wraps so 'of the year' is left alone on its own line. The date block is jammed right under the subtitle, and all the content is crammed into the top 60% of the canvas, leaving a large dead area below. The missing-asset placeholder is still visible. B: a faithful, cleanly ordered scale of the original with no collisions and correct hierarchy and grouping. However, it is mostly a shrunk copy rather than a real rearrangement: there is extra empty space above the logo and below the CTA, the chips and fine print are small at this size, and the missing-asset placeholder box is also still shown.

A: the big serif headline is clearly the focal point and the logo is intact. But the bottle shrinks to a tiny thumbnail jammed into the top-right corner, and the right column (body copy, CTA, legal) is tightly packed. The legal text is nearly as large as the body copy, and the ribbon floats between the two columns. B: the headline is shrunk to about body-copy size, so the hierarchy collapses. The logo and bottle are tiny and crammed together in the left column. The CTA isn't aligned with the centred headline or the body copy, and a large empty area sits at the lower right with only the small legal line in it.

A: the headline is undersized for a story, there's an odd gap between the headline and the body copy, the FREE DELIVERY badge floats loose next to the pills instead of sitting as a corner tag, and the bottom ~140px is dead space. B: hierarchy is stronger, with a larger product and headline and the badge kept in its original top-right spot. But alignment is mixed (GROVE centred, the copy left-aligned, the pills and CTA pushed right), the two pills almost touch each other and crowd the right edge, and the CTA cluster feels lopsided.

A actually re-lays out the design for the square: the headline is reset to four large lines and fills the canvas with strong hierarchy. Its weak point is the bottom row. The subline is centre-aligned inside a left column with a ragged wrap ('Now in / four flavours.'), its edge doesn't line up with the headline or the CTA, and the row sits tighter to the bottom edge than the headline does to the top. B is the original block re-centred at the same small size. It leaves about 210px of empty orange above and 240px below, the headline and CTA look undersized for the square, and the 16px subline reads like fine print, so it's a shrunk copy rather than a resize.

A is a clean vertical stack with no collisions and a centred CTA, but the 'WEEKEND ONLY' kicker has moved from above the headline to below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order. The body copy also wraps to leave 'sparkling.' alone on its own line, and the top band is mostly empty. B is broken: the bottle sits right on top of the copy, cutting off the 'f' in 'off' and hiding the end of 'Every mixed case of Solstice sparkling', and the bottom third of the canvas is dead space under the CTA.

A recomposes reasonably: the headline is large, the subhead sits under it, and the badge sits next to the CTA in a row. But the CTA and badge are jammed against the bottom and right edges, there is dead space at bottom-left under the subhead, and the phone sits tight on the left edge. B packs everything into the upper two-thirds and leaves a large empty orange band at the bottom. Its phone is small and pushed up near the top edge, and the tilted ONLINE ONLY badge nearly touches the CTA because it is stacked under it. The CTA cluster also crowds the right edge, so B looks unbalanced and unfinished.

A breaks up the original's order: the headline floats on the left with dead space around it, while the CTA is jammed under the product circle almost touching it and the bottom edge. 'Out now.' is cut off from the headline and squeezed next to the button. B keeps the original's left-to-right order of product, headline, then CTA, but has flaws: the product circle almost touches the top and bottom edges, the CTA is crammed against the right edge, and the button and 'Out now.' sit at staggered heights instead of on a shared grid.

A is mostly a shrunk copy of the original. Its hierarchy and grouping are intact, but the content sits high, leaving a dead lower third, and the 'missing asset' partner placeholder is still showing. B has a clear collision: the tilted can sits on top of 'Pier 9' and nearly touches the RSVP button. Everything in B is crammed into the top half, the date block nearly touches the subhead, and the bottom half is empty apart from the same broken placeholder.

A breaks the product graphic apart: the sage circle is stranded half off the canvas at the far left while the can floats on the right with empty space around it. Its text is crammed into the centre with SOLSTICE below the headline, which reverses the reading order, and the body copy is too small to read. The CTA is shrunk to badge size and lined up with the badges, so it no longer stands out. B reads left to right as a banner should: the can sits in its circle, then brand and headline, then copy with badges, then a prominent dark CTA at the right. Its only flaws are the very small can, the small body copy and the uneven gaps between columns.

A has no collisions, but the SOLSTICE wordmark sits awkwardly up and to the left of the headline instead of aligning with it. There is a dead gap between the phone and the text, the CTA is stacked under a badge at the same width so it barely stands out, the right ~170px is empty, and the subline is tiny. B has a clear collision: the 'Find It Near You' CTA covers the 'SUMMER ONLY' badge and cuts it off at 'SUMME'. Its CTA is also jammed against the right edge, the phone is cropped at the top and bottom, and the subline floats loosely above the badges.

A rebuilds the layout as a clean vertical story: the product sits in its circle on top, and below it the text is left-aligned with clear size steps and plenty of room. Its flaws are about 100px of dead space above the circle and a '20% off' headline that is a little small for this canvas. B blows the type up until it is cramped: '20% off' runs almost to the right edge, the subhead sits jammed against an oversized CTA, the circle is cropped off the top-right corner and pushed behind the text, and the product floats alone in empty space. The fine print 'Ends Sunday. Online only.' is set nearly as large as the subhead, so the hierarchy is broken.

A is basically the banner stacked into a left column. The bottle sits off-centre on the left edge of its circle, a small decorative circle floats with no purpose, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty. Its small 'Try It' button gets lost. B fills the square with a large two-line headline and a strong CTA, but it has flaws: the bottle cap nearly touches the top edge, and the circle is crushed into the corner. The left-aligned headline and right-aligned buttons share no common edge, and the NEW badge is oversized, so it competes with the CTA.

A: the headline's 'on 100 marathons' runs into the lime circle, putting white text on a light background with very poor contrast. 'Full review inside.' also sits on the bottom edge of the circle, and the lower ~40% of the canvas is empty. The NEW VIDEO badge is crammed into the top-right corner. B: the stack reads cleanly from logo and badge to a large headline, then the circle and shoe, then the subline. There are no collisions and the brand colours and proportions are kept. Small fixes: the VOLTSTRIDE logo is a bit small, and 'Full review inside.' sits tight against the circle and the bottom margin.

A reads left to right like a proper banner: the can sits inside its circle, then brand, headline, body copy with badges, and the CTA anchored on the right, where it is clearly visible. Its flaws are a very tiny can and cramped body copy and badges. B splits the circle (stranded at the far left) from the can (stranded at the far right), and puts the wordmark below the headline. Its CTA shrinks into a small pill at bottom-left that has the same weight as the badges, and the body copy is illegibly small, all crammed into the bottom row.

A has a real collision: the 'Find It Near You' button sits on top of the 'Summer Only' badge and cuts it off. The CTA text is also jammed inside its pill, and the phone is cropped at the top and bottom edges. B has no collisions, but 'SOLSTICE' is pushed right up against the headline, there's a dead gap between the phone and the copy, and the CTA is the same size as the badges, so it doesn't stand out.

A: the lavender circle is cut off from the product and now sits behind the headline, so 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off' land on it. The headline is oversized and runs almost to the right edge, the CTA is jammed under the subhead, and the product floats in a large empty middle with no anchor. B: the product sits back on its circle at the top and the text stack below is left-aligned with a clear hierarchy (eyebrow, headline, subhead, CTA, legal). Only small polish is needed: the copy block is a little compressed compared with the hero, and the legal line sits close to the bottom.

A fills the square with a bold headline and a strong CTA, but the bottle and circle are jammed into the top-left corner, with the cap almost touching the edge. The NEW pill is oversized and competes with Try It, and the right-aligned buttons don't share the headline's left edge, so the layout feels unanchored. B keeps one clean left column, but the whole design sits in the top 65%, leaving a large empty band at the bottom. The bottle also pokes out past the left of its circle, a stray decorative circle floats at top right, and the NEW and Try It buttons are undersized for the canvas.

A is a clean vertical stack: logo and badge on top, a large headline, then the shoe in its circle, then the subcopy. Its flaws are small: 'Full review inside.' sits close to the circle and the bottom margin is tight, and the badge is close to the right edge. B is broken: the headline runs over the lime circle and the shoe, and 'Full review inside.' sits on the circle. Everything is crammed into the top 60% of the canvas, leaving the bottom 40% empty, and the 'NEW VIDEO' badge touches the right edge.
